class.name: DisCollisionPdu
class.brief_description: Collision PDU (type 4): an entity collided with another entity or object.
class.description: A Collision PDU is issued by an entity that detects it has collided with another entity (or with something not known as an entity, in which case [member colliding_entity_id] is [code](0, 0, 0)[/code]). It is 60 bytes long and has protocol family 1 (Entity Information). [member velocity] is the issuing entity's velocity in the world (ECEF) frame in metres per second, [member location] is the point of impact in the issuing entity's body coordinates in metres, and [member mass] is the issuing entity's mass in kilograms.

method.name: decode
method.description: Parses [param bytes] as a Collision PDU and returns it. Returns [code]null[/code] and sets [method DisPdu.get_last_error] if [param bytes] is not a valid Collision PDU (header shorter than 12 bytes, wrong PDU type, protocol version outside 1-7, length field larger than [code]bytes.size()[/code], or fewer than 60 bytes). A length field of 0 is replaced by the datagram size. Bytes after the last known field, up to the length field, are kept in [member DisPduBase.trailing_bytes].

members.member: Entity ID of the entity that was hit; (0, 0, 0) if it is not a known entity as a [Vector3i] ([code]x[/code] = site, [code]y[/code] = application, [code]z[/code] = entity number).
Collision type (8-bit, SISO-REF-010 "Collision Type"): see [enum CollisionType].
Event ID as a [Vector3i] ([code]x[/code] = site, [code]y[/code] = application, [code]z[/code] = event number), unique per collision event of the issuing application.
Entity ID of the entity that issues the PDU, the one that detected the collision as a [Vector3i] ([code]x[/code] = site, [code]y[/code] = application, [code]z[/code] = entity number).
Location of the collision as a [Vector3] in metres in the issuing entity's body coordinates (32-bit floats on the wire).
Mass of the issuing entity in kilograms (32-bit float on the wire).
The 8-bit padding field after the collision type. Normally 0; kept so that decoded PDUs encode to the same bytes.
Velocity of the issuing entity at the time of the collision, in metres per second in the world (ECEF) frame (32-bit floats on the wire).

constants.constant: Inelastic collision (value 0): kinetic energy is not conserved.
Elastic collision (value 1): kinetic energy is conserved.
